text:
maya: quick sync: we prototyped a 'soft-tether' pattern where allocator marks spans with a lightweight policy tag (KEEP_LOCAL / SOFT_EVICT / MIGRATE_CANDIDATE) and the offload controller reconciles those tags rather than owning placement logic. pros: allocator can reason about fragmentation; controller stays stateless. cons?
luke: sounds promising. main con is convergence: two actors might disagree (allocator tags KEEP_LOCAL but controller is under pressure). need a tie-break rule.
trina: tie-break could be last-writer-wins with a monotonic epoch on the tag. but that means extra writes. maybe controller can carry a lease and only override if pressure score > threshold.
maya: proposal: tag = {action, score, epoch}. controller reads tag, computes pressure_score, and if pressure_score - tag.score > delta && epoch older than X then override. keep writes < 1 per second per span.
luke: delta needs calibration. in my bench a delta of 2000 (hotness units) avoided flipping during short spikes. also: define action semantics clearly: MIGRATE_CANDIDATE means prefer async copy then commit, SOFT_EVICT means drop backing pages and keep mapping with placeholder.
trina: for placeholder pages we must ensure page-fault path can reconstruct quickly; prefer a tiny bitmap + copy-on-demand mechanism. that avoids heavy synchronous compaction on hot paths.
maya: telemetry list: span_tag_changes, controller_overrides, migrate_bytes, evict_bytes, placeholder_fault_latencies. can we add quota_tag to track tenant-level cost shaping?
ops-bot: note: canary scheduled: soft-tether-v0 -> 10% @ 2025-10-28T03:00Z
luke: small API sketch (not proto, just idea):

```
SpanTag {
  enum Action {KEEP_LOCAL, SOFT_EVICT, MIGRATE_CANDIDATE}
  Action action;
  uint32 score; // higher => hotter
  uint64 epoch; // monotonic
  uint8 version;
}
```

trina: implementation: store tags in a side-channel table keyed by span id (64-bit) to avoid touching core page metadata. Use atomic CAS for updates.
maya: rollouts: feature-flag, instrument p99 fault latency, cross-tenant fairness check, and PCIe bandwidth ceiling. abort if migrate_bytes/min > threshold.
luke: question: eviction vs migrate cost model — should controller have a pluggable estimator that sums bytes*migrate_cost + expected_reloads*latency_cost? we need a simple formula initially.
trina: yes, start simple: cost = bytes * pcie_cost_per_byte + expected_faults * latency_penalty. expected_faults estimated from span.score decay history.
maya: adding doc-bot to capture this sketch in eng-runtime/designs. doc-bot: created draft: /docs/eng-runtime/soft-tether-offload.md
maya: thanks all, I'll follow up with a short RFC including the API, telemetry dashboard queries, and a microbench plan. ping me if you want to be on the canary list :slightly_smiling_face:
